summary: Iteration 31 — comprehensive backend testing of WanderMark moderation system (P0). Created /app/backend/tests/test_moderation_iteration31.py covering all 9 moderation endpoints, role-based gating (admin vs moderator vs user), suspension auth-block + super-admin bypass, hidden-content filtering on public feeds, and admin user filters (has_warnings, suspended). 26/26 moderation tests pass. Full regression: 264 passed / 1 flaky network failure / 2 skipped (baseline was 238/3 — net +26 from new moderation suite).

minor.issue: [FIXED by testing agent] TypeError 'can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes' on second+ warning. MongoDB returns naive datetimes for issued_at when read back, while thirty_days_ago is tz-aware. This caused 500 on every 2nd/3rd warning and would have completely broken auto-escalation in production. Fixed in /app/backend/routes/moderation.py by coercing naive datetimes to UTC-aware before comparison.

[OPTIONAL] Notification field naming inconsistency: helper stores type=<notif_type> in Mongo, but routes pass arg as `notif_type=`. Frontend / test queries should use the field name `type`, which is non-obvious. Consider renaming arg or adding a docstring.
critical_code_review_comments: BUG (fixed): warn_user() crashed with TypeError on subsequent warnings due to tz-naive Mongo timestamps vs tz-aware comparison. Auto-escalation logic would never have worked in real usage. Patch applied — wraps warning issued_at via _aware() coercion.
Suspension enforcement in get_current_user properly bypasses super-admin (role=='admin') so suspended super-admins can self-unsuspend. Verified in test_super_admin_bypasses_own_suspension.

Role gating is correct: get_admin_user accepts admin+moderator; get_super_admin_user requires admin only. DELETE /api/admin/content and GET /api/admin/moderator-activity correctly 403 for moderator role.
Hidden content is excluded from /api/community-highlights/top and /api/feed (verified live). Soft-delete preserves data for restore and audit (visit kept in DB with hidden=true).
Audit logging via _audit() runs after every destructive action — admin_logs collection has admin_id, action, target_id, meta, created_at — sufficient for compliance trail.
Suspension duration_days is correctly clamped to [1, 365] using max(1, min(days, 365)) — no negative or > 1 year suspensions possible.
moderation.py is 439 lines — within 700-line guideline. Single-responsibility (content + user mod actions co-located is acceptable).
The notification helper signature uses notif_type but stores under field `type` — minor naming inconsistency that could trip up future readers (cosmetic, not a bug).

rca of the issue: Bug RCA: routes/moderation.py line 222-225 — auto-escalation tried to count `recent_warnings` by iterating user.warnings[].issued_at and comparing to `thirty_days_ago = now - timedelta(days=30)`. `now` is tz-aware (datetime.now(timezone.utc)), but warnings retrieved from MongoDB lose tzinfo unless explicitly reattached, so the comparison raised TypeError on the 2nd+ warning. Reproduction: issue 2 warnings to any user → 500. Fix: added inline _aware() helper that does dt.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc) when dt.tzinfo is None before the > comparison. Mitigation: alternative is to configure motor with tz_aware=True at the client level — would benefit other endpoints too, but is a larger change. Recommended follow-up: add `tz_aware=True` to AsyncIOMotorClient in utils/db.py.
